observation.visible_scene: An open-ocean seascape under an overcast sky with a soft bright glow near the horizon. The sea fills the lower half of the frame with several swell lines and small whitecaps, and a band of white breaking foam crosses the foreground above a darker shallow-water edge at the very bottom.
visible_changes: Swell crests and small whitecaps drift steadily toward the lower-left of the frame (the left whitecap moves from roughly x=205,y=352 in frame 1 to x=100,y=380 in frame 41; a central whitecap from about x=540,y=345 to x=495,y=368), consistent with waves propagating toward the viewer.
The foreground foam line gradually advances downward, shifting from about y=430-450 in frame 1 to y=470-490 in frame 41, while its texture churns and reshapes.
The horizon line, cloud formation, and the bright glow near the horizon stay at essentially fixed screen positions throughout, indicating no appreciable camera pan or tilt.
Mid-distance dark swells rise and fall slightly in amplitude as the wave pattern moves, with no abrupt change or visible cut.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the wave set continues to break or recede after the last frame, and what preceded the first frame, is not shown.
The position of any shoreline or the observer's relation to the water is not visible.
uncertain_details: A very small camera drift cannot be fully excluded, but the static sky/horizon evidence suggests the camera is stationary.
The darker band at the very bottom may be shallow water over a beach or wet rock; its exact nature is not determinable.
Distinguishing individual wave periods from the continuous foam motion is approximate.
